systems.name: Massachusetts State Employees' Retirement System

statute.quote: The state employees' retirement system, the teachers' retirement system and all county, city and town contributory retirement systems, established under the provisions of this chapter, as existing on December thirty-first, nineteen hundred and forty-five, shall, subject to the provisions of sections one to twenty-eight inclusive, continue in operation

body.name: State board of retirement (Massachusetts State Retirement Board)

source.quote: The state employees' retirement system shall be managed by the state board of retirement provided for in section eighteen of chapter ten.

website_source.quote: The MSRB administers the Massachusetts State Employees' Retirement System (MSERS) for state employees and certain other employees of public entities.

systems.notes: Governed by G.L. c. 32. Judicial retirement benefits are also administered by the State Retirement Board.

systems.name: Massachusetts Teachers' Retirement System

statute.quote: The state employees' retirement system, the teachers' retirement system and all county, city and town contributory retirement systems, established under the provisions of this chapter, as existing on December thirty-first, nineteen hundred and forty-five, shall, subject to the provisions of sections one to twenty-eight inclusive, continue in operation

source.quote: The teachers' retirement system shall be managed by the teachers' retirement board provided for in section sixteen of chapter fifteen.

website_source.quote: Established on July 1, 1914, the Massachusetts Teachers’ Retirement System is the largest of the Commonwealth’s 104 contributory retirement systems.

covers_local_source.quote: a teacher, as defined in section one, shall be included in the teachers' retirement system, except that a teacher employed by the school committee of the city of Boston shall be included in the Boston retirement system

systems.notes: Covers teachers of city, town and regional school districts statewide except Boston.

systems.name: Berkshire County Retirement System

statute.quote: A contributory retirement system established for an abolished county operating under the terms of sections 1 to 28, inclusive, of said chapter 32 shall be known as a regional retirement system

source.quote: Said system shall be managed by a retirement board which shall have the general powers and duties set forth in subdivision (5) of section 20 of chapter 32.

website_source.quote: The Berkshire County Retirement System administers the pension system for the public employees of 46 towns, districts, and authorities throughout Berkshire County.

covers_local_source.quote: There shall be a regional retirement board advisory council consisting of all the treasurers, elected or appointed, of each town, unit, or district belonging to the prior county retirement system and remaining in the retirement system established by this section.

systems.notes: Former county system continued as a regional retirement system after county abolition; operates under G.L. c. 32 sections 1-28.

systems.name: Essex Regional Retirement System

statute.quote: The contributory retirement system for Essex county, operating under the terms of sections 1 to 28, inclusive, of chapter 32, shall be known as the Essex regional retirement system and all business shall be transacted under the name of the Essex regional retirement system.

source.quote: The Essex regional retirement system shall be managed by the Essex regional a retirement board which shall have the general powers and duties set forth in subdivision (5) of section 20 of chapter 32.

website_source.quote: The Essex Regional Retirement System provides retirement, disability and survivor benefits to approximately 1,800 retirees and 3,875 employees for 19 towns, five school districts, 17 housing authorities and six special districts throughout Essex County, Massachusetts.

covers_local_source.quote: The first member shall be a chief executive or chief administrative officer of a member town, unit or district belonging to the Essex regional retirement system for a term of 3 years.

systems.notes: Former Essex county system; operates under G.L. c. 32 sections 1-28.

systems.name: Massachusetts Housing Finance Agency Employees' Retirement System

statute.quote: The contributory retirement system established for the Massachusetts Housing Finance Agency under the provisions of sections one to twenty-eight, inclusive, shall be known as, and all of its business shall be transacted under the name of, the ''Massachusetts Housing Finance Agency Employees' Retirement System''.

body.name: Massachusetts Housing Finance Agency Retirement Board

source.quote: Said system shall be managed by an retirement board which shall have the general powers and duties set forth in subdivision (5).

website_source.quote: The Mass Housing Finance Agency Retirement System is a mandatory defined benefit retirement plan for nearly all full-time and part-time employees of the MHFA.

systems.notes: Employees of MassHousing, a state authority; G.L. c. 32 sec. 28(8) provides the agency's acceptance.

systems.name: Massachusetts Port Authority Employees' Retirement System

statute.quote: The contributory retirement system established for the Massachusetts Port Authority under the provisions of sections one to twenty-eight, inclusive, shall be known as, and all of its business shall be transacted under the name of, the ''Massachusetts Port Authority Employees' Retirement System''.

source.quote: Said system shall be managed by an retirement board which shall have the general powers and duties set forth in subdivision (5).

website_source.quote: The Massport Employees’ Retirement System provides Massport employees, past and present, and their beneficiaries with secure retirement, survivor, and disability benefits.

systems.notes: Employees of the Massachusetts Port Authority, a state authority.

systems.name: Massachusetts Water Resources Authority Employees' Retirement System

statute.quote: The contributory retirement system established for employees of the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority under sections 1 to 28, inclusive, shall be known as, and all of its business shall be transacted under the name of the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority Employees' Retirement System.

source.quote: The system shall be managed by a retirement board which shall have the general powers and duties set forth in subdivision (5).

website_source.quote: The MWRA Employees’ Retirement System is a contributory defined benefit plan which was established under C. 372 of the Acts of 1984, and which covers employees of the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority.

systems.notes: Created by St. 1984, c. 372 (a special act not in the statute index); named and governed by G.L. c. 32 sec. 20.

systems.name: MBTA Retirement Fund
systems.why: Not a G.L. c. 32 system: the MBTA Retirement Fund is a trust fund created in 1948 under a pension agreement between the transit authority's predecessor and its union; no establishing section found in the statute index (G.L. c. 161A sec. 50 only requires disclosure of MBTA retirement information).

website_source.quote: MBTA Retirement Fund – Building for the Future Since 1948

systems.notes: Census unit 'MBTA Retirement Plan'. Governed by a board under the pension agreement, not by statute.

systems.name: MBTA Police Association Retirement Plan
systems.why: Census unit 'Police Association Pension Plan (MBTA)' is a collectively bargained plan; G.L. c. 32 sec. 20 and 28 name an MBTA police retirement system, but it is not confirmed that this unit is that system, so no establishing statute is claimed.
systems.why_website: No official website found for the plan.
